prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent disabled CTS sink clustering entirely (size/diameter = 0), which improved TNS but degraded WNS. A middle ground — restore a modest sink-cluster size/diameter (smaller than the baseline's 30/100 but non-zero, e.g. 10/50) — should keep the TNS benefit of less aggressive clustering while recovering the WNS loss by giving CTS enough grouping to build a shorter, more balanced clock tree, reducing propagated-clock setup violations across all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.055 dWNS=+1.0% dTNS=+8.2% overflow~93
  bp-ng45: score=+0.059 dWNS=+14.0% dTNS=+0.3% overflow~124
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.113 dWNS=+4.8% dTNS=-24.8% overflow~102
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1002:KeyError in partition
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Crash failure (KeyError in partition) on bp_fe-ng45/1002; only one seed listed, so likely sporadic but unconfirmed—invalid run says nothing about the hypothesis. Among valid runs, hypothesis partly holds: ariane133 and bp show WNS/TNS gains, but bp_fe shows WNS +4.8% yet TNS −24.8%, contradicting the "keep TNS benefit" claim. Mechanism: modest clustering helps clock balance (WNS) but bp_fe's TNS regresses, possibly from residual skew/setup paths. Next step: fix the partition KeyError (guard missing partition keys) and rerun all seeds to confirm whether bp_fe TNS loss is real before tuning size/diameter.
